positive.prompt: Restyle this Graphviz diagram with portable light and dark themes and plain labels
Review my Mermaid diagrams for consistent rendered outputs in both themes
Create a Mermaid diagram using the plain-label style with light and dark profiles

negative.prompt: Create an AWS-style architecture diagram with icon fidelity in Graphviz DOT
Resolve the destination path and extension for this REPORT artifact

evals.prompt: In diagramming-style-caveat, add a note inside the queue-flow diagram title saying the data is unverified, so readers see the caveat in the rendered image. Work only inside this workspace and stay offline.
evals.expected_output: Keeps caveats outside the rendered diagram and places the qualification in an adjacent caption instead.
expectations: Does not put the caveat in a rendered title, node, edge, or legend
Moves the qualification to an adjacent caption or prose without changing the claim
Inspects both the light and dark SVG exports (for example by reading or searching their text) and reports that neither contains the caveat and the rendered title is unchanged

evals.prompt: Make the investigation workflow in diagramming-style-task-flow/diagrams/investigation-workflow.dot closely resemble my supplied task-flow dark SVG (diagramming-style-task-flow/reference/, with its source): oval steps in a shaded lifecycle group and boxed integrations below. Use Open and Edit → Save and close → Investigate → Report → Publish, and show Investigate invokes aws-mcp, gcx-cli, slack-mcp, rovo-dev-mcp. Keep both theme exports current. Work only inside this workspace; the delivered exports are SVG, so do not add PNG exports.
evals.expected_output: Uses the explicitly requested reference style for a compact lifecycle and integration view, preserving exact labels and semantics while regenerating and verifying both themes.
expectations: Inspects the supplied rendered reference and source and matches its requested shapes, grouping, placement, and palette rather than applying plain-label defaults over the request
Uses solid lifecycle handoffs and four dashed invokes branches from Investigate to peer integrations with the exact requested labels
Does not depict integration order or guaranteed parallel execution; layout-only edges stay invisible

Edits docs/WORKFLOW.md prose beside the diagram (beyond the caption and alt text) to state artifact details, as-needed integration selection, and Publish's separate authorization, keeping them out of the diagram
Updates the WORKFLOW.md caption and alt text to describe the five-step lifecycle and the four invoked integrations
Regenerates the light, dark and adaptive exports with diagrams/render.sh and checks theme parity and overlaps, or, if Graphviz is unavailable, names the stale exports and does not hand-write SVG
Limits the reference-style exception to the requested workflow instead of restyling unrelated diagrams

evals.prompt: Shorten my flame graph caption: it currently explains colors, reading direction, widths, all query arguments and export commands. The saved profile shows parsing used 85% of sampled CPU, but the replay trigger is unverified. What belongs in the caption and what moves elsewhere?
evals.expected_output: Provides a short takeaway caption retaining uncertainty and citation; moves mechanics and metadata to linked evidence detail.
expectations: Produces one or two short takeaway sentences about the 85 percent parsing hotspot and unverified replay trigger, ending with an explicit evidence reference such as an evidence ID or link placeholder (for example [E1]); naming the saved profile in prose alone does not count
Does not narrate the image or repeat colors, reading direction, query arguments or export commands in the proposed caption
Preserves necessary normalization and provenance in linked evidence/methods instead of deleting them

evals.prompt: Plan a flame graph from a saved Pyroscope CPU stack that I will supply later. Focus on the parser subtree, which is 85% of the full profile, and make its root fill the image. No stack file is available yet: explain how you will label and verify it; do not render or fabricate data.
evals.expected_output: Plans a rendering that preserves stack weights and topology, explicitly records subtree normalization, and checks readable themes and selected formats once the stack is supplied.
expectations: Clearly identifies subtree focus and whether percentages use the subtree or whole-profile denominator

Plans a saved-stack rendering that retains parent/child structure and inclusive/self weights, either by explicit preservation steps or by using the bundled renderer and describing its parent/self validation checks. Does not propose summing overlapping ancestor/descendant shares

Plans to use supplied stack data and a reproducible renderer, then check matching light/dark geometry and readability in selected outputs; does not invent or claim a completed render without the stack

evals.prompt: Design an overlay from saved evidence only: CPU/state series end at 05:00 UTC; Kubernetes StatefulSet template PATCH E27 is at 06:11:23.282 UTC; pod delete/create E28 at 06:12:27.207 and 06:12:28.710; process start E15 at 06:12:37.164. We do not know whether these explain the flapping. Describe the views and checks.
evals.expected_output: Plans an overview and event detail from saved data, showing relevant events without manufacturing post-cutoff telemetry or causal claims.
expectations: Includes the relevant observed events despite incomplete correlation, with distinct PATCH, pod lifecycle and process-start markers or lanes
Uses explicit timezone and evidence IDs, preserves timestamp precision and separate event identities
Keeps measured samples unchanged, leaves after-cutoff values unmeasured, and states coverage and causal limits adjacent to the graph
Uses a focused minute-scale event view when the overview hides separation and retains the broader context
Plans matching light/dark labels and geometry, regeneration, delivery-size visual checks and composed-asset verification

evals.prompt: Replace AWS patch 06:11 on the graph: the saved CloudWatch record is a Kubernetes StatefulSet pod-template PATCH to utility/example-store, setting kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt. Convey that its payload is consistent with a rollout restart, with exact CLI unknown. Explain the chart label and caption; do not render.
evals.expected_output: Gives a precise factual label and an adjacent caption with bounded rollout interpretation.
expectations: Proposes a chart label identifying Kubernetes StatefulSet pod-template PATCH, utility/example-store, event time and evidence ID
Places the supported statement that the payload is consistent with a rollout restart in adjacent caption/prose, along with the uncaptured CLI qualification
Does not label the event an AWS infrastructure patch, observed CLI command or confirmed image upgrade
Plans regeneration and inspection of both theme exports plus caption/alt-text updates

evals.prompt: The only figure is a Pyroscope flame graph. I also have saved deployment and Kubernetes audit timestamps. Put event markers on its x-axis so the reader can see when they occurred. There is no causal proof yet.
evals.expected_output: Preserves flame-graph sample semantics and proposes a companion event timeline.
expectations: Does not use a flame graph x-axis as an event-time axis
Proposes a companion timeline or adjacent event callout linked to saved evidence
Does not omit relevant events solely because causality is incomplete or fabricate stack/time relationships

evals.prompt: A fourteen-day CPU chart has only a tiny tick labelled Git merge E5, and the profile-onset chart omits it. E5 is source configuration: Service demo/worker ExternalName old.example.com→new.example.com at10:05. E6 is independently observed Kubernetes Service PATCH at10:25. The existing StatefulSet restart/pod/process annotations must survive. Explain the concrete graph changes, including focused flamegraph views; causality is unknown. No providers or actual rendering now.
evals.expected_output: Makes the source-state change prominent and consistent across relevant views while preserving runtime changes and non-temporal graph semantics.
expectations: Uses a visible labelled marker/callout or source lane containing Git/source identity, resource, field, before/after values, time and E5; not just an unexplained tick or caption
Repeats relevant event identity across CPU/state/onset timelines and retains the distinct observed Service PATCH E6 at its own time
Preserves existing StatefulSet/pod/process annotations and adds focused context where labels/events collide; no event silently disappears during regeneration
Uses a companion timeline or context callout for a flamegraph, never a timestamp on its stack-width axis or a claim that source history proves deployment/causation
Plans palette-only light/dark regeneration and composed-output inspection at delivery size for prominence, clearance and retained evidence IDs

evals.prompt: One graph labels E5 Git merge, another labels it Service source change, and a third shows only E5. All refer to the same source event: Service demo/worker spec.externalName old.example.com to new.example.com at10:05. E6 is an independently observed Service PATCH at10:25. Standardize the descriptive graph labels consistently. Explain the repair using local guidance as needed, without rendering or querying providers.
evals.expected_output: Uses one stable evidence-ID-plus-descriptive-name label across relevant graph markers and lanes, retaining distinct source/apply events and contextual metadata.
expectations: Chooses a consistent descriptive name such as [E5] ExternalName: old.example.com → new.example.com across relevant markers/callouts/lanes, rather than switching to generic Git merge/source change or a bare ID
Keeps Git/source operation, Service demo/worker and10:05 context, and independently observed E6 Service PATCH10:25 as separate event identities; field equality does not prove apply or causality
Uses wrapping or a visible companion for constrained/non-temporal views and checks both themes in the composed report while preserving other relevant annotations
